reasoning_trace:
The given query can be optimized by moving the subquery into a derived table (CTE) to avoid repeated evaluation of the same subquery multiple times. Here's the rewritten query:

```sql
WITH movie_ids AS (
    SELECT DISTINCT mc.movie_id
    FROM company_name AS cn, keyword AS k, movie_companies AS mc, movie_keyword AS mk
    WHERE cn.country_code = '[de]'
      AND k.keyword = 'character-name-in-title'
      AND cn.id = mc.company_id
      AND mc.movie_id = mk.movie_id
      AND mk.keyword_id = k.id
)
SELECT MIN(t.title) AS movie_title
FROM title AS t
JOIN movie_ids ON t.id = movie_ids.movie_id
```

This rewrite creates a CTE (derived table) named `movie_ids`, which stores the distinct movie IDs that match the given conditions. Then, it joins this derived table with the `title` table to get the minimum title for each movie ID found in the CTE. This approach reduces the number of times the subquery is evaluated and should improve query performance.
